reviews.text: I was always a sucker for time-travel movies and the mind-bending paradoxes that materialise from baffling scenarios of crafty science fiction.
reviews.author: Wael Khairy

reviews.text: Ultra-seasoned sci-fi that turns into a turmoil of reflections... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: An inventive, mid-budget sci-fi thriller that laid the groundwork for Johnson's mainstream success...
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: Looper never focuses too much on sci-fi because the film keeps our attention on the old-school action-thriller taking place on the screen.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: It’s cerebral yet filled with substantial dramatic pull, exploring both brainy scientific theory and multidimensional characters with equal levels of inspection and inventiveness.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: “Looper” takes the familiar device of time travel to new places through a brilliantly original concept.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: ... the smartest science fiction thriller of 2012.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: another feather in the cap of a writer/director who knows how to play with expectations, how to set up details without heavy obviousness, and to lead with emotion in order to invest his audience.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: [A] compellingly original sci-fi starring.
reviews.author: George Fenwick

reviews.text: Looper joined Moon, Inception, Interstellar and Source Code in proving that the thinking-person's sci-fi, last truly prominent in the 1970s, came back with a vengeance during the past decade.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: The action, drama, suspense, and performances are all entertaining, but at the end, it's impossible not to come back to the faults in the film's time travel foundation.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Easily One of 2012's Best Sci-Fi Flicks.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Fantastic performances, big ideas, and the ability to pull off a slick narrative juggling act.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: This is the kind of science fiction that can be seen multiple times. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: If you pick too much around the edges of LOOPER, it will inevitably fray slightly, as do many intricate time travel yarns. However, LOOPER is a layered and intelligent neo-noir science fiction with some striking images and emotional resonance.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Complex, entertaining yet brimming with intelligence, Looper needs to be watched - easily one of the smartest films this year.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Rian Johnson, director of Brick and The Brothers Bloom, has bit off a big honkin' chunk of sci-fi mythology with Looper.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: A mind-bending bit of science-fiction entertainment -- a trippy piece of cinema with an equal mix of style and substance.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: A very original sci-film with a creative premise and story.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Looper embraces the paradox that's required for the two-Joes story to even happen, knotting improbability, vengeance and the notion of choice into a taut, sleek, imperfect but intelligent action movie.
reviews.author: Molly Templeton

reviews.text: For all its promise, Looper is a true film of two parts (halves wouldn't be quite accurate in terms of narrative focus) -- with the second, ultimately, a jumbled genre-clash of misfires and missteps.
reviews.author: Daniel Green

reviews.text: Looper is solid in performance, action and effect, with some admirable surprises along the way and at the end.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: [Writer-director Rian Johnson] is one of the most stylish young filmmakers working today.
reviews.author: Kelly Jane Torrance

reviews.text: While this latest time-travel movie isn't perfect, it is a thought- provoking, intelligent story with heart.
reviews.author: Debbie Baldwin

reviews.text: Films like Looper are the reason spoiler tags were invented. This is a film that demands to be seen cold and discussed later.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Some may try to nitpick the film to death ... but look past the little details and you'll find a film that, as a whole, is both fun and thought provoking.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Looper may not be something Christian moviegoers want to expose themselves to, but it should hearten us to know that young, influential filmmakers like Johnson are wrestling with these questions in such well-done movies.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: There isn't one wasted moment or word.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: A breath of fresh air as we creep into the heavy fall dramas and awards glitz, Looper will likely not be forgotten as the film that showed up and got the job done.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: Great set-up. Awful follow-through.
reviews.author: Rebecca Pahle

reviews.text: While the film overshoots its landing by a mile, it's a worthwhile science fiction piece with no shortage of interesting ideas.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Rian Johnson is a very clever man, if sometimes a bit too clever for his own good.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: This is the real deal, folks - intelligent, humorous, exciting entertainment that happens to be sci-fi but is by no means limited to that genre's target audience in terms of appeal.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: This is a wildly entertaining film that isn't content with science and cinematic tricks. It desires, and achieves, much more.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: I found myself dreaming of the days when Willis would take a rest from Die Hard-ing to do character cameos of unexpected depth and pathos: Pulp Fiction, Nobody's Fool, and a few others. Now he clings to stoic longevity, and shoots people.
reviews.author: David Thomson

reviews.text: The ending is both daring and logical, two rarities in modern sci-fi.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: With a heady script, stunning performances and fist-pumping action, LOOPER is the most enjoyable combination of immensely watchable yet poignant, even cerebral.
reviews.author: Meredith Borders

reviews.text: If it weren't for its gaping plot holes, this could be one of this century's best science fiction features.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: A fresh, intelligent and action-packed addition to the time-travel anthology.
reviews.author: Tom Glasson

reviews.text: Not quite the time travel story science fiction fans were hoping for, alas.
reviews.author: James O'Ehley

reviews.text: Yes, it's a B movie sci-fi thriller, but not many prestige pictures have this much going on underneath the surface.
reviews.author: Tom Charity

reviews.text: [Looper] may be the best sci-fi thriller to hit the theaters since 1995's Twelve Monkeys.
reviews.author: Michael Burgin

reviews.text: That first hour cooks. And the second hour brings Emily Blunt into the story, which is a fine thing for any second half to offer.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Is it derivative? Not really; just a reminder that cinema, like history, is on a continuous loop, forever repeating itself.
reviews.author: Peter Keough

reviews.text: Despite its confusing logic and ornate storyline, Looper still grabs the audience with the raw emotional storyline on the farm and the constant popping back and forth in time. It's a head-scratching ride, but a fun one nonetheless.
reviews.author: Matthew Odam

reviews.text: Call it the coolest, most complex sci-fi of 2012 and the best movie of its kind since "Inception." Pow! What a ride!
reviews.author: Paul Chambers

reviews.text: Accessible to a general audience while still having moments that will warm any film geek's heart, this is the kind of genre film that elevates the form.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: The movie is morally murky, to put it lightly, and that's a bit refreshing; we're made to think about why we want the protagonists to achieve their goals.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Intelligent, extremely imaginative, visually stunning and constantly surprising, this is filmmaking of the highest order from Rian Johnson.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Looper is among the cleverest, most skillfully crafted and entertaining sci-fi thrillers of the past 20 years.
reviews.author: Jay Antani

reviews.text: The smartest, most stylish and most outright entertaining science-fiction film of the year.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: A thought-provoking, heart-pounding take on the applications and ethics of time travel which, oddly enough, doubles up as a lesson in the importance of good parenting.
reviews.author: Film4 Staff

reviews.text: This is one of those rare genre movies (like the original TERMINATOR) that reminds us that Sci-Fi can be smart. It's much more than just a bunch of special effects and explosions. It's what all movies should aspire to be.
reviews.author: Austin Kennedy

reviews.text: While it sometimes feels like it's trying to do much, Looper manages to be a creditable and exciting sci-fi flick that homages the past while carving out a unique identity.
reviews.author: Laurence Boyce

reviews.text: Much as he did in Brick, Johnson creates a carefully drawn world in Looper that exists by its own particular set of rules.
reviews.author: Jason Buchanan

reviews.text: ... has an irresistible energy and a don't-give-a-damn unpredictability ...
reviews.author: Jim Lane

reviews.text: Beautifully crafted, acted and written.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: Anchors high-concept thrills and captivating ideas in a world of challenging morality and intricate personal consequences.
reviews.author: Tom Clift

reviews.text: Truly imaginative but all the twists and turns make the overall film difficult to follow. Plus Gordon-Levitt has not reached leading man status yet.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Kind of a reverse-"Terminator" without any of James Cameron's wit (or wisdom),
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: An endlessly creative mind-blowing film that captures everything right about the movie going experience. Johnson conjures up the most imaginative action/science fiction film since 'Inception.'
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Part science fiction, part mob movie, and with a nice infusion of dark comedy at just the right moments, Looper is Johnson's best movie yet, and manages to be hugely entertaining, affecting, and thought-provoking.
reviews.author: Ian Buckwalter

reviews.text: takes us far beyond the film's high-concept premise into the kind of emotional terrain that too often escapes even the best genre filmmakers
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Doesn't quite reach the heights of the lofty ideals that it so ardently seeks to expound, but makes up for this with the sheer thrill of the journey Rian Johnson takes us on.
reviews.author: Steve Wright

reviews.text: Ingenious with a fine performance by Emily Blunt, but far too much cold-blooded violence.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Engaging, exciting, and successfully cross-breeding elements of Terminator and even Pet Sematary, Looper is a solid work of palatable science-fiction.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: Looper's super. An action-thriller that bothers to have a brain.
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: Looper may not take us back to the future as satisfyingly as Robert Zemeckis' Marty McFly trilogy or James Cameron's Terminator franchise, but writer-director Rian Johnson does enough right to all but guarantee that he has a future cult film on the books.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The best time travel films play on emotion rather than logic, and once Looper realises this and drops all the tail-chasing about how time travel works it settles into the engrossing action/drama about destiny it should have been from the get go.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Has more depth, smarts, and heart than the usual sci-fi bluster.
reviews.author: Tricia Olszewski

reviews.text: A just about brilliant sci-fi crime-drama-thriller mostly set in the years 2044 and 2074. Rian Johnson is a rare director who creates entertainment with depth.
reviews.author: John Wirt

reviews.text: The key to enjoying the gruesome violence mixed with a healthy potion of emotional depth rarely found in this genre is to not dwell on the fiction in the science.
reviews.author: Bruce Bennett

reviews.text: Sometimes time travel is just used a cheap device in movies to make them seem different; this is not one of those films. It's genuinely unique and fresh.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: Very entertaining on many, many levels.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: The best kind of light entertainment that expects you to be just as intelligent as it is.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: It's complex enough that sci-fi fans can dig deeper over multiple viewings, but thrilling enough that casual viewers can take it all in with one watch.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: ...an above-average sci-fi tale.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Rian Johnson makes a loud, dark, highly stylized film that looks good but whose ideas do not really bear close examination.
reviews.author: Mark R. Leeper

reviews.text: Time travel makes sense in Looper because writer-director Rian Johnson keeps it on a short leash, not requiring enough manufactured logic to trip over later.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: I don't know where you guys found that kid... Was it the same lab where they grew the Fannings?
reviews.author: Widgett Walls

reviews.text: Besides a challenging time-travel premise, a dark sense of humor, and some thrilling action scenes, Looper has the kind emotional weight that you wouldn't expect.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: ... Writer-director Rian Johnson never stops working, using the science-fiction setup and trappings to delve into the characters and give us a story with some real meat.
reviews.author: Greg Maki

reviews.text: You don't need time-travel to spot a future cult classic.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: It's just a shame that a smart, thoughtful movie like this is all too often the exception to mainstream sci/fi action fare rather than the rule.
reviews.author: Ethan Alter

reviews.text: Despite some big set pieces, it's the smaller emotional moments that get us thinking
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Nothing less than an exceptionally satisfying piece of futuristic ingenuity with a great corps of actors. It will knock you out -- in any time zone.
reviews.author: Jules Brenner

reviews.text: The reasoning behind all this may not reward prolonged inspection, but Johnson is smart enough to press onward with his plot, leaving us with neither the time nor the desire to linger over the logic ...
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: A scintillating neo-noir gem of existential quandaries and inescapable fatalism.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Joseph Gordon-Levitt, the hardest working man in Hollywood for 2012, continues his journey to the A-List.
reviews.author: Scott Nash

reviews.text: Best stay focused and avoid a loo break!
reviews.author: Pauline McLeod

reviews.text: This all sounds a little too much like The Terminator, but Johnson keeps things moving and rings ingenious changes on familiar material ...
reviews.author: Philip French

reviews.text: Do make time for it.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: It might be confusing in its time-travel material, but is both entertaining and somewhat challenging by being so action-packed and loopy.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Refreshingly unique
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: "Looper" is frenetic, loud, creative, entertaining and, of course, unbelievable.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: ... re-establishes the (time travel) genre in a new and fresh way. And seriously, how cool is it to have an actual blunderbus for an assassin's weapon?
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Exciting and engrossing futuristic thriller - with a solid payoff.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Time travel is tricky. Even more tricky than talking time is reviewing Looper and not giving away the tasty time treats awaiting serious and non-serious sci-fi fans.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Well-constructed narrative, looping back on itself, spiraling willingly into its own paradoxes and dealing with all the weird overlaps in a way few movies dare to bother with.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: A sci-fi action thriller that's smart, complicated, and that actually follows through on plot twists guaranteed to make the audience uneasy.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Johnson's direction builds on the optimistic tone that is inherent in the best time-travel stories: the idea that there are always second chances to fix past mistakes.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Like any good piece of speculative fiction, "Looper" can't be boiled down into a short plot blurb... There hasn't been a movie quite like it.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Keeps you mentally hopping, daring you to guess where it is headed, then cheerfully pulling the rug out from under you each time.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: this is nothing less than a consideration of how at every moment, every person on the planet is making one of an infinite number of choices that will lead to an infinite number of possibilities. It's enough to make the head spin. And it does. Sublimely.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: One of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: Joshua Tyler

reviews.text: A mind-bending ride that is not afraid to slow down now and again, to explore themes of regret and redemption, solitude and sacrifice, love and loss. It's a movie worth seeing and, perhaps, going back to see again.
reviews.author: Christopher Orr

reviews.text: Looper is an ambitious undertaking. The (slightly) flawed result stands heads above as an example of quality sci-fi crafted by an artistic and creative filmmaker.
reviews.author: Kofi Outlaw

reviews.text: Looper is a thoughtful genre-bender that brings science-fiction, action and mystery together in one tight package.
reviews.author: Tyler Hanley

reviews.text: Awards talk is way premature. But giving a solid, mostly original genre entry its due praise is not.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: A stunner from start to finish -- a smart, exciting time-travel action film that respects its audience, its genre and even its characters.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Looper has more heart than Brick and the 2008 con-man flick The Brothers Bloom. Both fine achievements, they could also be described as viscerally cerebral.
reviews.author: Lisa Kennedy

reviews.text: While Gordon-Levitt and Willis have a blast with the space-time issues and some funny dialogue, the movie loses steam after a solid start.
reviews.author: Lori Hoffman

reviews.text: I'm a sucker for time-travel movies.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Looper is like a Christopher Nolan movie with a sense of humor.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Looper is a thinking man's science fiction film with a bold plot that grabs you from the opening frame.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: The subplot revolving around Cid takes away from the sci-fi and time travel yarn, taking me out of the loop, so to speak.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: An ingenious, witty film that simply brims with ideas and energy.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Other films evoked by 'Looper' include Brian De Palma's 'Carrie' and, inevitably, Terry Gilliam's '12 Monkeys' (1995), which also stars Willis and which is light years ahead of 'Looper.'
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Looper does a better job of making sense of the nonsensical than any time-travel film since Shane Carruth's undervalued Primer.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Unusal and Intriguing
reviews.author: Diana Saenger

reviews.text: So close to being a great movie is Looper that I want to go back in time and chat with writer-director Rian Johnson about the parts of the film that come up short.
reviews.author: Jeff Meyers

reviews.text: I'm definitely going to see "Looper" again. But you know what I want even more than that? I want to go back in time, and experience it for the first time again.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: The most robust pure sci-fi in years - tighter and more fun than even 'Inception', if not as dizzyingly ambitious in its engineering.
reviews.author: Eugene Novikov

reviews.text: More than just being atmospheric, "Looper" also delivers some awesome action sequences and novel plot twists ... This is a movie that sticks with you and is fun to talk about after the fact.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Ambitious to a fault, but Johnson's vision remains original and initially hypnotic, constructing a wild but winded tale of time travel -- one of the rare movies this year with almost too much minutiae to manage successfully.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Mind-bending science-fiction and proud of it, not just a Western set in outer space or a monster movie set on an alien planet. It's worth seeing twice.
reviews.author: Matt Soergel

reviews.text: As sturdy as it is stylish -- but most of all flat-out entertaining.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: "Looper" is the best action/sci-fi film in years.
reviews.author: Jolene Mendez

reviews.text: Looper felt to me like a maddening near-miss ...
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: It's a head flip of a time trip.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Writer-director Rian Johnson has come up with a nifty sci-fi hook, and he keeps as tight a rein as possible on the story's twisty internal logic.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: ... a smart and sharply realized vision of a not-too-distant, not-too-dystopian future [that] doesn't get too fussy with the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: The transgression of internal logic suspends a faithfully observant viewer's disbelief more than Mr. Gordon-Levitt's glued on eyebrows.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: This is an exciting, exceptionally well-made futuristic thriller that also happens to be loaded with lived-in touches and punchy ideas.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: Boasts Rian Johnson's reverence for cinema past while taking genre movies into a promising future. Looper is that rare thriller that always stays ahead of its audience. You may feel like you need a time machine just to catch up to it.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: A fashionably sleek, unfashionably smart science-fiction film that tick-tick-ticks along with pocket-watch precision.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Johnson doesn't explain too much, but he explains just enough about how two people can be one person, and how the younger entity's actions, in real time, can affect the memory of the older entity.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: While the third act inevitably bogs down a bit in gunplay and chases, there are more than enough moments of visual wonder and storytelling surprise to make it worth the trip.
reviews.author: Marc Mohan

reviews.text: The smart idea at the center blossoms into an equally smart movie.
reviews.author: Rob Vaux

reviews.text: As with his brilliant and ground-breaking "Brick," also starring Gordon-Levitt, writer/director Rian Johnson has an engaging and compelling way of mixing genres.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Looper is a challenging, fun, serious and action packed movie in all of the right ways.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: Johnson - who collaborated with Levitt on his brilliant debut thriller Brick - has crafted both an intelligent and compelling sci-fi world.
reviews.author: Alex Zane

reviews.text: [It] may begin as a "Terminator"-like piece of time travel escapism, but ultimately gathers Old Testament-worthy force and fury.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: An indie-inflected popcorn movie with major brains, brilliant acting and a highly satisfying payoff, "Looper'' is the first must-see movie of the season.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: "Looper" looks like and is a blast; what's really cool is it's even more than that.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: Johnson's action scenes occasionally stumble, but the devilishly clever script makes "Looper" a thrilling, dizzying ride.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Looper provides some breathtaking moments of action and food for thought, although we'd go easy on the latter.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: The dialogue is as clever as the conceit.
reviews.author: Rick Groen

reviews.text: While "Looper" lacks the heft of a classic, this wayback machine is worth taking for a spin.
reviews.author: Joe Williams

reviews.text: You'll be unravelling its time travel machinations in your head as you walk from the cinema, but there are some scenes that will live much longer in the memory.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Looper is a rare example of ingenious science-fiction storytelling where the fundamental concepts are so intriguing that their stylish execution feels like gravy.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: From the carefully choreographed action scenes to the themes of revenge and redemption, Looper is the work of a visionary. Don't miss it.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Looper marks a significant step forward for time-travel storytelling. Johnson's outstanding vision and execution push at the genre's emotional and psychological boundaries harder than any sci-fi work in recent memory.
reviews.author: Jonathan Lack

reviews.text: It's official: Looper closes the loop on any doubt that writer/director Rian Johnson is one of the most fascinating filmmakers to appear on the doorstep of the 21st century.
reviews.author: Kimberly Gadette

reviews.text: A really fresh and innovative spin on the genre that, although it doesn't quite result in the next great sci-fi classic, is definitely one of the better contemporary films of its kind.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: While there are problems aplenty with the logic (or lack thereof) of the plot's various elements and devices, I still managed to be caught up in the characters and the story as they played out. (Full Content Review for Parents also available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Brutal and chilling, if not air-tight, it is best to allow the many pleasures of "Looper" to sweep over without dwelling too closely on particulars.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: The result is a film that is simultaneously a visceral and an intellectual experience.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The leads blend as seamlessly as any young-old character coupling I've seen.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: This is a genuinely tough-minded and unpredictable movie, one of the fall's most enjoyable entertainments ...
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: The first half of writer/director Rian Johnson's film is gripping, but by the second half it's all become unbelievably confused and disjointed.
reviews.author: Claudia Connell

reviews.text: It will likely have moviegoers gathering outside the theater afterward to hash out details of its intricately constructed universe.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: This is a highflying, super-stylish science-fiction thriller that brings a fresh approach to mind-bending genre material.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Faintly absurd, but done up with such confidence that you're willing to go along for the ride.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It's safe to predict that "Looper" will transform Mr. Johnson's career, and give pleasure to popeyed audiences for a long time to come.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Mr. Johnson throws a lot at the screen, blasted corpses included, yet little here is as initially transfixing as Mr. Gordon-Levitt's mug.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Even with its echoes of sci-fi thrillers past, from La Jette to The Terminator, Rian Johnson's mind bender feels fresh - fresh enough to be forgiven for sputtering off the rails in the final act.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: Johnson is strong enough to come in with a great conceptual finish, one which links his loopers to a more universal 'cycle of vengeful violence.'
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: However long it takes to get your bearings, Looper is worth it. Bruce Willis expertly blends tough and tender and Joseph Gordon-Levitt is at the top of his game in this rip-roaring mind-bender.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: "Looper" pedals furiously and largely successfully to keep our disbelief from crashing to the ground.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: "Looper" shows a good deal of evidence of [Johnson's] ability to deal with complex issues in an engaging manner, but it also shows that he knows how to put together an intriguing story with the material.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: There hasn't been much lately for those who crave some brain power along with their effects-driven firepower. Now comes Looper, the time-travel tease from Rian Johnson that is an immensely fun yet thought-provoking ride.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: "Looper" is a superior genre film, an engrossing thriller that engages not only the senses, but our minds as well, just as good sci-fi should do.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Looper is a self-consciously good-looking, profoundly silly movie that nevertheless comes off as high-minded.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Looper grounds itself in the commonplace realities of moments ... and then takes off on wild flights of science fiction-y suspense. The combination is cool.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: A gripping time-travel, sci-fi thriller indebted to Christopher Nolan's Memento and James Cameron's The Terminator, but with its own creepiness and muscular sense of urgency.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: For sci-fi nuts, Looper corrects the past.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: Despite the movie's downbeat view of the life-is-cheap future, it's a kick to watch, and makes a virtue of its bleakness by virtue of amusing performances.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: [Johnson] uses speculative and film noir elements to defy expectations of both.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: The second Rian Johnson movie in a row (following The Brothers Bloom) that looks great but meanders while doing it.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Looper isn't just the smartest, most ambitious film I've seen in 2012, it's something more: it's one of my favourite films of all time.
reviews.author: Adam Ross

reviews.text: Matching its intelligent and taut thrills with richly developed characters and thought-provoking questions, this is one of the decade's best sci-fi flicks.
reviews.author: Erin Free

reviews.text: Looper is a dark, violent and surprisingly intelligent edge-of-your-seat thriller with a similar feel to sci-fi trips like Inception and In Time.
reviews.author: Adam Bub

reviews.text: With just his third feature, Looper's writer-director Rian Johnson reveals himself to be the most exciting and unorthodox filmmaker to splash into the mainstream since Christopher Nolan.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: It's an intriguing ride and I really enjoyed it. I think it's clever.
reviews.author: Margaret Pomeranz

reviews.text: A playful sci-fi thriller on the tantalising theme of time travel and how the future can be altered.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Looper may be as flawed as hell... but it has enough brilliance to get it over the hump.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: The dystopian setting... makes for some bold cultural commentary, but as usual with Johnson, the engaging ideas feel like affectations rather than products of a fully developed sensibility.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: Once you envision how ridiculous the Tinseltown version of this tale would be, what director Rian Johnson accomplishes is all the more special.
reviews.author: Bill Gibron

reviews.text: Yet another rehash of the first "Terminator" film, revisiting the time travel genre without bringing a whole lot new to the table.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: With his third film, writer/director Rian Johnson has crafted his most mainstream picture to date, without sacrificing one whit of the dazzling inventiveness or finely detailed characterizations that distinguished his earlier pictures.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: Gordon-Levitt is flinty, and Willis, on his A-game, is fiery. Together, they take us on a helluva trip.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: A for effort. C and see-me for results and how to improve them for the DVD.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: A fanciful film with the patina of hyper-realism, Looper is well served by actors who behave not as if they were dropped carelessly into the future but spent their whole desperate lives there.
reviews.author: Richard Corliss

reviews.text: Not just a great movie but a great movie that seems to promise more great ones to come.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The most resourceful, vivacious and savage science fiction movie of 2012.
reviews.author: Adam Lee Davies

reviews.text: Though this is a shadowy, violent film, Johnson wisely inserts just enough humor to create shades of gray rather than blackness.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: A bold, ambitious sci-fi drama that is destined to be more admired than adored.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: A very fulfilling sci-fi adventure that certainly knows how to close the loop.
reviews.author: Mark Sells

reviews.text: "Looper" is a welcome return to smart science fiction. It's more than just a popcorn film. It's a drama that uses an age-old genre device to play a fantastic moral game of cat and mouse. A definite must-see.
reviews.author: Justin Craig

reviews.text: Johnson knows what he wants you to think about, and he expects you to relax and enjoy the rest. You can draw the diagrams later.
reviews.author: Loey Lockerby

reviews.text: This is a "you know what would be cool?" movie that considers the real-world ramifications of its science-fiction whiz-bang, and a film of ideas that doesn't skimp on the action.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: "Looper" weaves between past and present in a way that gives Johnson and his actors opportunities to create a surprisingly involving narrative.
reviews.author: Roger Ebert

reviews.text: Loopers really need to unionize.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: ...a muddled echo of several other films where the filmmakers treated their ideas as something more than a gimmick.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: For all its weighty genre trappings, Looper is really about that existential connection, and in that it mostly succeeds.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: All of Looper's ideas, elements and actions loop back on themselves to create a thrilling, fascinating and fiercely imaginative head-scratcher that's undoubtedly the best sci-fi of 2012.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: Rian Johnson...has conjured a supremely well-crafted science-fiction thriller that fully delivers on the promise of its out-there premise.
reviews.author: Simon Foster

reviews.text: Intriguing conversation material but curiously cold and unsatisfying as drama.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: A stylish, intelligent and superbly acted Sci-Fi thriller with some intriguing ideas and great dialogue ...
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: Looper imagines a world just near enough to look familiar, and just futuristic enough to be chillingly askew.
reviews.author: Lisa Schwarzbaum

reviews.text: I knew this was my kind of sci-fi movie when Bruce Willis yells at Joseph Gordon Levitt, insisting that they stop talking about how time travel works and just get down to the business at hand.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: A nifty time-travel thriller that hits the mark.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Good news: Not only is the smart, sexy, sophisticated but still slam-bang sci-fi action-thriller not dead, it's just gotten itself a potent shot in the arm by way of writer-director Rian Johnson.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: The best advice is to not overthink "Looper," as Johnson's already done that. Instead, just sit back and enjoy it.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: A clever, clever contraption about trading in your future to feed your present, and the lost boys and regretful men who willingly embrace such a bargain already believe they have nothing to live for or look forward to.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Looper is so bursting with its own ideas, it is easy to miss how cannily Johnson references other movies.
reviews.author: Rob Daniel

reviews.text: Looper is up there with Duncan Jones' Moon and Source Code in the ranks of this century's most genuinely exciting sci-fi films.
reviews.author: Emma Dibdin

reviews.text: The finish is the cinematic equivalent of David Tyree's Super Bowl catch; a conclusion that miraculously - magnificently - manages to close the final loop with an off-the-Richter-scale stroke of genius.
reviews.author: Erick Weber

reviews.text: As in the very best Anthony Mann and John Ford westerns, Looper at once understands the visual power of violence and is deeply critical of it.
reviews.author: Chris Cabin

reviews.text: Johnson's brilliant move is to center his sci-fi around a basic human survival drama.
reviews.author: Justin Strout

reviews.text: Johnson establishes the machinery of the time-travel concept, then steadily pushes it into the background in favor of exploring his characters and the difficult questions they face.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Looper is a tremendous motion picture experience. Not merely a "very good" one, but a great one.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: It's nice to have a movie worm its way into your brain and leave you wondering and wanting more, and for the mechanics of the plot hold up to further scrutiny. Joseph Gordon-Levitt's fake eyebrows, I suspect, would not withstand such close examination.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Will render any blubbering sci-fi fan speechless.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: It isn't flashy and has no intentions of outsmarting the viewer. Johnson presents a world that's wholly digestible, but ever changing, forcing you to keep on your toes.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: In short, for all its affectionate pastiche, Looper is a humanist movie, and is all the better for it.
reviews.author: Nick Pinkerton

reviews.text: Looper tries (and fails) for a love-against-all-odds resonance, but the shortcomings are minimal. Johnson's still got plenty of unlooped time to grab that brass ring.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: This is a hugely satisfying, enjoyable and thought-provoking piece of work.
reviews.author: Tom Huddleston

reviews.text: Gritty action sequences, striking visuals, and a superbly clever script. One of the better sci-fi films of the last decade without breaking a sweat.
reviews.author: Brian Salisbury

reviews.text: Mostly avoiding the trip-wires of illogic that tend to plague the gobbledygook of time travel, Johnson dodges the bullet by veering away from plot twists and special effects and instead focusing on relationships, character and emotions.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: As well-staged as some of the action is, it often comes down to gunplay, which is never particularly interesting ...entertaining if not exactly gripping.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: If high-toned futuristic time-travel pictures with a splash of romance float your boat the way they do mine, you'll have yourself a time.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: [VIDEO ESSAY] As time-travel suspense thrillers go "Looper" is a pinch better than mediocre.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: It's a thriller with fantasy elements and if you disregard (or don't care about) the internal confusion of its world, you may find it works for you
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: Looper continually messes with your head as the future physically catches up with the past... I love the boldness of the concept
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: Looper is a delicious movie with some imaginative curveballs ...
reviews.author: Siobhan Synnot

reviews.text: Looper isn't perfect, but it pulls off the full Wizard Of Oz: it has a brain, courage and a heart.
reviews.author: Kim Newman

reviews.text: A mind-bending masterpiece that's a must for more cerebral fans of the time-travel genre.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: Bruce Willis and Gordon Levitt render terrific, complementary performances in Johnson's third and most fully realized feature, which delivers as sci-fi, thriller and actioner!
reviews.author: Emanuel Levy

reviews.text: "Works on so many levels" is sort of an inside joke among film critics. No joke here; Looper really does.
reviews.author: Scott Weinberg

reviews.text: A delight, a revelation of imaginative storytelling. Willis delivers his most assured performance in years.
reviews.author: Ed Gibbs

reviews.text: It's energizing to watch a fast-paced action film that challenges the audience. The intricate, intelligent storyline demands that you pay attention at all times.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Takes the best elements of time manipulation and brings those ideas together in a volley of bullets and drama. Wildly entertaining and satisfying for the psyche.
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: From the room-silencing blunderbuss bang of the first execution, Looper's pleasures are plenty.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: A disappointment from an ingenious and intelligent filmmaker
reviews.author: Sam Fragoso

reviews.text: An outlandish vision of the near-future which may defy credibility but is bracingly entertaining.
reviews.author: Kevin Lally

reviews.text: The smartest movie of the year and the best action movie of the year.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: A mishmash of futuristic conventions and clichés cobbled together as something we have never quite seen before.
reviews.author: Chris Laverty

reviews.text: Rian Johnson's 'Looper' is one of the year's best films... a huge jump forward for a filmmaker whose first two films both exhibited a strong, clear voice.
reviews.author: Drew McWeeny

reviews.text: Nothing quite excites and disturbs us as the prospect of time travel. Looper exploits that tension for all its worth.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Looper is a classic piece of sci-fi cinema, riddled with brilliant ideas, a complex and satisfying narrative and, most importantly, a heartbeat.
reviews.author: Jon Lyus

reviews.text: There's a bit of Twelve Monkeys, more than a dash of Terminator 2.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: An electrifying time-travel thriller worthy of comparison to THE TERMINATOR.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Spectacular. Packed with intelligence and feeling. The year's most excitingly original movie.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Savvy, nasty fun, then, and seeing Brucie still able to pull off the tough guy is a form of time travel all in itself.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: "Looper" is thrilling to watch even when it falls apart.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: It is personal, dark, daring, weird, and refreshingly unique. It is also one of the best sci-fi films of the last several years.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: A spectacularly cool time-twisting sci-fi thriller.
reviews.author: Mark Adams

reviews.text: The most ambitious, inventive, downright invigorating film you're likely to see all year. Original science fiction film-making at its very finest.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: Johnson hauls us through a cat-and-mouse chase, peppered with great dialogue and two showcase performances from Willis and Gordon-Levitt, who's nailed the pained look of befuddlement, the mannered slouch in the walk, that made Willis a star.
reviews.author: Henry Barnes

reviews.text: Thoughtful, intimate, and deeply moving, writer-director Rian Johnson's assured and perfectly-measured third feature is one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Stitched together with dynamism and precision
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: The coolest, most-confident sci-fi flick since 2006's 'Children of Men.'
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Looper is one of the year's most engaging sci-fi films, one that works as both a thriller and a character piece about people faced with making big life decisions (often at the business end of Blunderbuss).
reviews.author: Jim Vejvoda

reviews.text: [Rian Johnson's] grandly conceived, impressively mounted third feature shows a giddy, geeky interest in science-fiction, then forces it into the back seat and lets the multidimensional characters drive.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Rian Johnson's third and most ambitious feature keeps the action popping while sustaining interest in the long arc of a story about a man assigned to kill the 30-years-older version of himself.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: One of the best films of 2012. You'll immediately want to see it again.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: "Looper" successfully closes its loop. For some, that will be enough. But the screenplay takes a few shortcuts to reach its destination, hiding behind the truth that when the future is unpredictable, present day is allowed to be vague.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: It feels like something new and different. Futuristic, even.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Creates a world so lively and well-wrought I'd happily see a dozen more movies set there.
reviews.author: Katey Rich

reviews.text: A hugely ambitious and mind-blowing sci-fi twist on the gangster flick that's likely to make it one of the coolest movies of the year.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

synopsis: In a future society, time-travel exists, but it's only available to those with the means to pay for it on the black market. When the mob wants to eliminate someone, it sends the target into the past, where a hit man known as a looper lies in wait to finish the job. Joe (Joseph Gordon-Levitt) is one such hired gun, and he does his job well -- until the day his bosses decide to "close the loop" and send Joe's future self (Bruce Willis) back in time to be killed.
